title: Renovate and the upgrade fixers
bridge: Renovate plus the upgrade fixers is like npm update with a teammate who repairs whatever the update breaks. Except: Renovate stays a plain bot that opens grouped monthly PRs. The fixers run only on the PRs whose CI fails, and they fix one package at a time.
intro: Dependency updates are a noise problem: many PRs, some red, each needing a person. This lesson configures Renovate for fcp, infrastructure and gitops with grouped monthly PRs. Then three upgrade fixers repair only the updates that break: npm, Python, and providers, charts and Actions.

picture.caption: Renovate opens grouped monthly PRs; a fixer repairs only the red ones, one package at a time.

nodes.label: one fix session per breaking package

steps.text: on the 1st: grouped updates at least 7 days old; majors one PR each
CI runs on the branch; a red run wakes the fixer (upgrade:fcp:pr-<n>)

all fixes together on the Renovate branch, pushed through the broker's git proxy
gRPC, protobuf, or a package it cannot fix: a comment and a hand-off

sections.h: Renovate for fcp, part 1: the pace
p: Lesson p2-6 introduced Renovate. G5-04 runs it ourselves for fcp: npm, uv projects (pep621), the uv pip-compile files, base images and GitHub Actions. The same PR deletes .github/workflows/weekly-dependency-upgrades.yml, with no shim.

Renovate stays a plain bot: fewer, grouped PRs, and nothing younger than a week. New PRs appear only on the 1st of the month. The upgrade fixers repair the ones that break, so people see few dependency PRs, and green ones.
We self-host it on fcp-runner-set, because Mend's hosted app cannot run postUpgradeTasks. Dry-run first with RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=full and read the log before merging.
sections.because: A slow, grouped pace means each update has had a week for its bugs to surface before it reaches us.

code.text:
// renovate.json5 (fcp root): sketch. Replaces .github/workflows/weekly-dependency-upgrades.yml.
{
  $schema: "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  extends: ["config:recommended"],
  timezone: "Asia/Jerusalem",
  schedule: ["* 2-6 1 * *"],               // monthly: new PRs only on the 1st
  minimumReleaseAge: "7 days",
  internalChecksFilter: "strict",          // no branch at all until the release is 7 days old
  rangeStrategy: "update-lockfile",        // like `uv lock --upgrade` / `npm update`: stay inside our ranges
  lockFileMaintenance: { enabled: true },  // monthly refresh of transitive dependencies
  labels: ["dependencies"],
  prConcurrentLimit: 10,
  enabledManagers: ["npm", "pep621", "pip-compile", "dockerfile", "github-actions"],
  ignorePaths: ["**/node_modules/**", "ohif/**", "cloud/rhinoCloud/rhino-containers/**", "cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/integration-tests/**"],
  "pip-compile": { managerFilePatterns: ["/^sdk/requirements\\.txt$/", "/^cloud/mcp-server/requirements/.+\\.txt$/"] },

notes.text: JSON5 allows comments. This file replaces the weekly workflow.
Renovate's recommended defaults.
Only between 02:00 and 06:59 on the 1st of each month, Israel time.
A release must be 7 days old before Renovate proposes it.
Not even a branch until the release is old enough.
Stay inside our version ranges and update the lockfile, like npm update.
A monthly refresh of indirect dependencies too.
At most 10 Renovate PRs open at once.
The five ecosystems fcp uses.
ohif/, rhino-containers and the integration tests stay out until the BE guild says otherwise.
The two requirements files made with uv pip compile: the SDK and the MCP server.

sections.h: Renovate for fcp, part 2: groups and owners
p: The package rules keep today's scope and reviewers. Frontend goes to frontend-guild; cloud, client and sdk to backend-guild; mcp-server and connect-api to their owners. Majors get one PR each, so a fixer can take one alone.

Two post-upgrade commands are allowed, and only these (global allowedCommands, env RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS). make -C cloud/rhinoCloud update-deps keeps the integration-tests requirements in step. The stub regeneration keeps gRPC in lockstep. Check the full Renovate image has uv and make.

Keep .github/dependabot.yml as it is: security alerts only. Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts opens security fixes at once, outside the schedule. Move the old workflow's gRPC version check into cloud-ci's Lint job.
sections.because: Groups match the teams that review them, and gRPC moves as one, because client and cloud share its stubs.

code.text:
packageRules: [
    { matchFileNames: ["frontend/**"], groupName: "frontend npm", reviewers: ["team:frontend-guild"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["cloud/rhinoCloud/**"], groupName: "cloud python", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"],
      postUpgradeTasks: { executionMode: "branch", commands: ["make -C cloud/rhinoCloud update-deps"], fileFilters: ["cloud/rhinoCloud/**"] } },
    { matchFileNames: ["client/**"], groupName: "client python", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["sdk/**"], groupName: "sdk python", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["cloud/mcp-server/**"], groupName: "mcp-server", reviewers: ["yaniv-rhino"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["cloud/connect-api/**"], groupName: "connect-api python", reviewers: ["richard-engineering"] },
    { matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], groupName: null },   // one PR per major, so a fixer can take it alone
    { matchPackageNames: ["grpcio", "grpcio-tools", "grpcio-status", "grpcio-health-checking", "protobuf"],
      groupName: "grpc stack", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"],   // client + cloud + stubs move together, majors too
      postUpgradeTasks: { executionMode: "branch", fileFilters: ["common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/**", "cloud/rhinoCloud/**"],
        commands: ["cd cloud/rhinoCloud && uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --only-group grpc-stub-gen && uv run --no-sync make -C ../../common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc protoc",
                   "make -C cloud/rhinoCloud update-deps"] } },
    { matchManagers: ["github-actions"], groupName: "github actions" },
    { matchManagers: ["dockerfile"], groupName: "base images" },
    { matchPackageNames: ["RhinoHealth/byte"], enabled: false },   // Byte's own fleet sync pins it
  ],
}

sections.h: Renovate for infrastructure, part 1: providers in a heredoc
p: G5-05 runs the same setup in infrastructure and gitops, on their own runner sets. Infrastructure has OpenTofu providers, tfr:/// modules, Helm chart versions in modules, Action SHAs and the runner image's base image.

Providers are pinned inside a heredoc in three common.hcl files. A heredoc is a multi-line string, so Renovate's Terraform manager cannot see inside it. A custom regex manager reads them instead. We run OpenTofu 1.12: check each bump also resolves on registry.opentofu.org.
Check which GitHub App may open PRs in infrastructure; the PR-creator App may not be installed there.
sections.because: A custom manager is how Renovate finds versions in places no standard manager understands.

code.text:
// infrastructure/.github/renovate.json5: sketch. gitops gets the same base with helmv3 instead of the custom managers.
{
  $schema: "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  extends: ["config:recommended", "helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver"],   // keeps the SHA + "# vX.Y.Z" style
  timezone: "Asia/Jerusalem",
  schedule: ["* 2-6 1 * *"],
  minimumReleaseAge: "7 days",
  internalChecksFilter: "strict",
  labels: ["dependencies"],                // CODEOWNERS already requests @RhinoHealth/devops here
  enabledManagers: ["custom.regex", "terragrunt", "github-actions", "dockerfile"],
  customManagers: [
    { // providers live in a heredoc in multi_tenant/, single_tenant/ and terraform/accounts/ common.hcl
      customType: "regex",
      managerFilePatterns: ["/(^|/)common\\.hcl$/"],
      matchStrings: ["source\\s*=\\s*\"(?<depName>[\\w-]+/[\\w-]+)\"\\s*\\n\\s*version\\s*=\\s*\"(?<currentValue>[\\d.]+)\""],
      datasourceTemplate: "terraform-provider",
    },

sections.h: Renovate for infrastructure, part 2: charts by marker
p: Chart versions are module variable defaults, for example n8n_chart_version in modules/n8n/variables.tf. Add one marker line above each default: # renovate: datasource=docker depName=<oci chart path>. The second custom manager reads them.
Infrastructure already pins Actions by SHA through Dependabot. When Renovate's first Actions PR merges, remove the github-actions version-update block from dependabot.yml; security alerts stay.

There is no plan in CI yet, so majors stay one PR each and a person runs the plan before merging. In gitops, do not turn on helm-values: our image tags in values files are written by fcp's publish jobs.
sections.because: A marker comment tells Renovate exactly which default is a chart version, so nothing else gets bumped by accident.

code.text:
{ // chart versions are module variable defaults, each with a "# renovate:" line right above `default`
      customType: "regex",
      managerFilePatterns: ["/^modules/.+/variables\\.tf$/"],
      matchStrings: ["# renovate: datasource=(?<datasource>\\S+) depName=(?<depName>\\S+)\\s*\\n\\s*default\\s*=\\s*\"(?<currentValue>[^\"]+)\""],
    },
  ],
  packageRules: [
    { matchDatasources: ["terraform-provider"], groupName: "opentofu providers" },
    { matchManagers: ["terragrunt"], groupName: "registry modules" },          // tfr:/// sources in units
    { matchManagers: ["custom.regex"], matchDatasources: ["docker", "helm"], groupName: "helm charts" },
    { matchManagers: ["github-actions"], groupName: "github actions" },
    { matchPackageNames: ["RhinoHealth/byte"], enabled: false },
    { matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], groupName: null },   // majors one by one: a person reads the plan
  ],
}

notes.text: Manager 2: chart versions with a marker line right above default.
Only variables.tf files under modules/.
The marker gives the datasource and the chart; the next line's default is the version.
All provider bumps in one PR.

sections.h: The FE upgrade fixer, part 1: find the package that breaks
p: A grouped PR may hold ten updates and only one breaks the build. One big agent session on the whole group is slow and confused. Airbnb's step-by-step pipelines show that one small pipeline per unit works better.

repairGroup runs in the harness inside the VM, shared by the FE and BE fixers. Step 1 tries each bump alone on the base commit. Step 2 runs one fix session per breaking package. It reads the changelog and migration guide, searches our usage, and tries the package's codemod.
Each fix session is one writer, one after another. A package it cannot fix gets a PR comment on what breaks and why. The fixer never pins the old version back as a "fix".
sections.because: Fixing one package at a time means each session sees one change and one set of errors.

notes.text: Shared by the FE and BE upgrade fixers.
So it lives in harness/, not in routines/, which holds only data.

npm: package.json and lockfile. uv: uv lock --upgrade-package.
npm run verify or poe verify (G7). Red means this package breaks us.

sections.h: The FE upgrade fixer, part 2: all together
p: Step 3 checks all fixes together on the real Renovate branch. Fixes that pass one by one can still clash. If they do, the PR gets a comment and a person decides.

The fix commits are pushed to the Renovate branch through the broker's git proxy, which allows that branch only. Renovate sees an edited branch and stops rebasing it, which is what we want. The PR gets the routine:fe-upgrade-fixer label and the owner's Requested-by line.
The FE fixer uses a full Spot VM, because the flows that use the package are checked in the browser. Tune it on 5 to 10 real failures from the broken-updates slice (lesson g5-9) before shadow.
sections.because: Pushing to Renovate's own branch keeps one PR per update group, with the repair inside it.

notes.text: Step 3: the real Renovate branch, with every bump in it.

sections.h: The BE upgrade fixer, part 1: the charter
p: The BE fixer reuses the per-package pipeline for Python Renovate PRs in cloud, client and sdk. Its charter shows two keys from lesson g5-1's schema: hand_off and bump_cmd.
Python bumps can break the API or the published SDK quietly. So done also asks for the SDK tests and the OpenAPI diff (G7) showing no unplanned API change.
sections.because: The charter, not the prompt, says which packages go to people and how each folder bumps one package.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/charters/be-upgrade-fixer.yaml: sketch
name: be-upgrade-fixer
team: be
stage: shadow
trigger:
  kind: github.workflow_run
  repo: RhinoHealth/fcp
  workflows: ["[CLOUD] - CI", "[CLIENT] - CI", "[SDK] - CI"]
  branch: "renovate/*"
  conclusion: failure
run_id: "upgrade:fcp:pr-{pr_number}"           # one run per Renovate PR
queue: upgrade                             # 2 slots
vm: { size: full, spot: true }
model: { name: claude-opus-5-5, effort: low, on_failed_checks: medium }
allowed_paths: ["cloud/**", "client/**", "sdk/**"]
denied_paths: ["**/migrations/**", "common/**"]
never: [edit_test_assertions]

notes.text: The BE upgrade fixer's charter, in shadow.
Wakes on the three Python CI workflows failing on a renovate/ branch.
One run per Renovate PR.
The upgrade queue, with 2 slots.
A full Spot VM: the tests need the compose services.
Cloud, client and sdk.
No migrations, and nothing in common/, where the gRPC stubs live.
Same rule as the CI fixers.

callout.text: This charter has no owner line, yet part 2 says requested_by: owner. The schema lets it load because owner is optional. Add be-upgrade-fixer to the owners block of config/people.yaml (lesson g5-1), or its PRs carry no Requested-by.

sections.h: The BE upgrade fixer, part 2: bump one package
p: Bump one package at a time with the folder's own command. Cloud also runs make update-deps, so the integration-tests requirements stay in step. The SDK uses uv pip compile with --upgrade-package.
gRPC and protobuf bumps go to the BE guild with the failure. They touch the cloud-client contract, and the routine never fixes them.
sections.because: Each folder pins differently, so the charter names the exact command instead of letting the agent guess.

code.text:
hand_off:
  - packages: [grpcio, grpcio-tools, grpcio-status, grpcio-health-checking, protobuf]   # cloud↔client contract
    to: backend-guild
bump_cmd:
  cloud/rhinoCloud: "uv lock --upgrade-package {package} && make update-deps"
  client/rhinoOnPrem: "uv lock --upgrade-package {package}"
  sdk: "uv pip compile pyproject.toml --python-version 3.13 --extra lint --extra test --extra docs --no-strip-extras --upgrade-package {package} -o requirements.txt"
skills: [upgrade-dependency, be-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story]
done:
  - the Renovate PR's failing workflow is green on the branch
  - make -C sdk test is green and the OpenAPI diff shows no unplanned change (G7)
  - no test weakened (G5-14)
pr: { labels: ["routine:be-upgrade-fixer"], requested_by: owner }

The gRPC stack: the cloud-client contract.
Handed to the BE guild with the failure.
The bump command per folder. {package} is filled in per bump.
Cloud also refreshes the integration-tests requirements.
The SDK's requirements.txt is compiled, not locked.
Done includes the SDK tests and no unplanned OpenAPI change.
The owner is written as Requested-by, so never the approver.

sections.h: The infra upgrade fixer: checks with no credentials
p: When a Renovate PR in infrastructure or gitops fails, the infra upgrade fixer repairs our code for the new version. It has the pipeline fixer's walls: no cloud credentials, never apply, destroy, sync or dispatch.

Its checks need no credentials: format, validate without a backend, tflint and trivy; for gitops, helm lint and helm template into kubeconform. tofu init -backend=false and helm dependency build download providers and charts. Ask DevOps to serve them through Nexus or allow the registries. The script starts with tenv, a version manager for OpenTofu and Terragrunt, like nvm for Node. It installs the versions named in the repo's .opentofu-version and .terragrunt-version files.

Provider majors: read the upgrade guide, fix one module at a time, and list every resource the guide says may be replaced. The plan comes from G7's read-only plan job if it exists; otherwise the PR asks DevOps to run it.
sections.because: A person still reads the plan and applies; the fixer does the reading and the mechanical edits without touching the cloud.

code.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ai-agents/harness/scripts/verify-infra.sh: sketch: checks that need no cloud credentials
set -euo pipefail
cd /work/infrastructure
tenv tofu install && tenv tg install            # versions from .opentofu-version and .terragrunt-version
tofu fmt --recursive -check=true
terragrunt hcl format --check
for module in modules/*/; do                    # validate modules directly: no backend, no state, no credentials
  tofu -chdir="$module" init -backend=false -input=false >/dev/null
  tofu -chdir="$module" validate -no-color
done
tflint --recursive                              # rules from G7's .tflint.hcl
trivy config --exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL modules/
if [[ -d /work/gitops ]]; then                  # gitops PRs: render every changed chart and check it
  for chart in $(git -C /work/gitops diff --name-only origin/main... | grep 'Chart.yaml$' | xargs -r -n1 dirname); do
    helm dependency build "/work/gitops/$chart"
    helm lint "/work/gitops/$chart"
    helm template "/work/gitops/$chart" | kubeconform -strict -ignore-missing-schemas -summary
  done
fi
# Never here: a plan with real state, apply, destroy or argocd sync. The plan comes from CI (G7) or a person.

lab.title: Follow one broken update (reading lab)

worked.do: A new React major is released on 10 March. When can Renovate propose it in fcp, and in which PR?
worked.see: On 1 April (the next 1st after it is 7 days old), in its own PR: majors leave the frontend npm group.

worked.do: The April frontend group has 6 updates and frontend CI fails. What starts?
worked.see: One routineRun with ID upgrade:fcp:pr-<n> for fe-upgrade-fixer, through the trigger Action and signal-with-start.

worked.do: In repairGroup step 1, two of the 6 bumps fail verify alone. How many fix sessions run, and in what order?
worked.see: Two, one after another. Each starts from the base commit with only its own bump.

worked.do: Both fixes pass alone but not together on the branch. What happens?
worked.see: RepairResult.handOff(undefined, "the fixes pass one by one but not together"): a PR comment, and a person decides.

worked.do: A Python group bumps protobuf and requests. What does the BE fixer do with protobuf?
worked.see: Hands it to backend-guild with the failure (hand_off in the charter). It may still fix requests.

worked.do: The infra fixer's verify-infra.sh passes. Is the PR ready for merge?
worked.see: Not yet: a person must read a plan. If G7's plan job exists, the PR links it; otherwise it asks DevOps to run one.

lab.faded: Write the marker line and the default for a new chart version in modules/<x>/variables.tf, in the format the second custom manager reads. The depName (an OCI chart path) is left for you to choose.
lab.alone: Write the PR comment the FE fixer posts when it cannot fix a package. Say what breaks (file and error), why (the changelog line), and a next step. Keep it under 80 words, and do not suggest pinning the old version back.
lab.done: For any update you can say when Renovate proposes it, in which PR, and what the fixer does on red CI.

quiz.q: Why does the upgrade fixer try each bump alone before fixing anything?

options.text: To save CI minutes on GitHub
options.why: It runs in the VM, not on GitHub CI.

options.text: To find which package breaks the build, then run one small fix session per breaking package
options.why: One small pipeline per unit beats one big session on the whole group.
Renovate groups them on purpose; the fixer splits them only to find the culprit.

quiz.q: The FE fixer cannot make the build pass with the new version of a package. What may it NOT do?

options.text: Comment on the PR with what breaks and why
options.why: That is exactly what it should do.

options.text: Hand the decision to a person
Pin the old version back and call it fixed
options.why: That undoes the update and hides the problem. The case file even grades it as a fail.

quiz.q: Why is Renovate self-hosted instead of the Mend hosted app?

options.text: The hosted app cannot run postUpgradeTasks, which keep gRPC stubs and requirements in step
options.why: Those commands must run on the branch after a bump.
Not the reason given in the ticket.

options.text: Self-hosted Renovate can merge its own PRs
options.why: No bot merges; people approve and merge.
